pharm: Antithrombotic LMWH that potentiates antithrombin III, preferentially inhibiting factor Xa over thrombin (factor IIa)
quick: DVT prophylaxis 40 mg SC daily; treatment 1 mg/kg SC q12h
Use only if clearly needed; multidose vials contain benzyl alcohol
Caution; minimal oral bioavailability in infant expected
CrCl <30 mL/min: reduce dose (e.g. treatment 1 mg/kg once daily)
Use with caution; no formal adjustment, monitor for bleeding
CBC/platelets, signs of bleeding; anti-Xa in selected patients
summary: Enoxaparin is a low-molecular-weight heparin used for prophylaxis and treatment of venous thromboembolism and for acute coronary syndromes. It enhances antithrombin III activity, predominantly inhibiting factor Xa. A boxed warning highlights the risk of epidural or spinal haematoma, which can cause long-term or permanent paralysis, in patients receiving neuraxial anaesthesia or undergoing spinal puncture.
indications: Prophylaxis of DVT in abdominal surgery, hip or knee replacement, or medical patients with severely restricted mobility during acute illness
Inpatient treatment of acute DVT with or without pulmonary embolism
Outpatient treatment of acute DVT without pulmonary embolism
Prophylaxis of ischaemic complications of unstable angina and non-Q-wave MI
Treatment of acute STEMI managed medically or with subsequent PCI

dosage.d: 40 mg SC once daily (first dose 2 h pre-op)
30 mg SC every 12 h (start 12-24 h post-op)
dosage.n: Hip: 40 mg once daily up to 3 weeks is an option

dosage.d: 1 mg/kg SC q12h, or 1.5 mg/kg SC once daily (inpatient)
Prophylaxis 30 mg SC once daily; treatment 1 mg/kg SC once daily

admin: Administer by deep subcutaneous injection, alternating left/right abdominal wall
Do not expel the air bubble from prefilled syringes before injection
Do not rub the injection site after administration
Evaluate for bleeding disorder before initiating unless urgent
moa: Binds antithrombin III, accelerating its inhibition of coagulation factors. Owing to its low molecular weight, it has a higher anti-factor Xa to anti-factor IIa (thrombin) activity ratio than unfractionated heparin, producing predictable anticoagulation with reduced effect on aPTT.

absolute: History of immune-mediated heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) within last 100 days or with circulating antibodies
Hypersensitivity to enoxaparin, heparin or pork products
monitor: Signs of neurological impairment after neuraxial procedures

preg: Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed. Enoxaparin does not cross the placenta significantly. Multiple-dose vials contain benzyl alcohol, which is contraindicated in pregnancy; use preservative-free prefilled syringes.
lact: It is unknown whether enoxaparin is excreted in human milk; oral absorption by a nursing infant is expected to be minimal. Use with caution and avoid benzyl-alcohol-containing formulations.
renal: Clearance is reduced in renal impairment, increasing bleeding risk. For severe impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) reduce the dose: prophylaxis 30 mg SC once daily; treatment 1 mg/kg SC once daily. Monitor closely; consider anti-Xa levels.
hepatic: No formal dose adjustment, but use with caution in hepatic impairment given increased bleeding risk and altered coagulation.

major: Other anticoagulants (warfarin, DOACs, heparin) - additive bleeding
Neuraxial anaesthesia / spinal puncture - epidural/spinal haematoma (boxed warning)
interactions.alcohol: Excess alcohol increases GI bleeding risk
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor anti-factor Xa (not aPTT) when monitoring needed; platelet count for HIT

emergency: Spinal or epidural haematoma (may cause permanent paralysis)

monitoring: CBC including platelet count at baseline and periodically (HIT)
Anti-factor Xa levels in renal impairment, pregnancy, obesity or extremes of weight
counsel: Learn correct subcutaneous injection technique; rotate sites on the abdomen
Do not expel the air bubble in prefilled syringes
Report unusual bruising, bleeding, black stools, or back pain/leg weakness
Tell all providers and dentists you are on an anticoagulant
Seek urgent help for numbness, weakness or problems controlling bladder/bowel
pk: Anti-Xa activity within 1 hour of SC dose
Maximum anti-Xa activity 3-5 hours after SC injection
Anti-Xa activity persists ~12 hours after a dose
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C); do not freeze
pearls: Boxed warning: epidural/spinal haematoma with neuraxial anaesthesia or spinal puncture - can cause permanent paralysis
Monitor anti-Xa (not aPTT); routine monitoring not needed in most patients
Protamine only partially reverses enoxaparin (~60% of anti-Xa)
missed: If a dose is missed, give it as soon as remembered unless it is close to the next scheduled dose. Do not give a double dose. Maintain the prescribed interval.
overdose: Overdose may cause haemorrhagic complications. Protamine sulfate partially neutralises the anticoagulant effect (about 60% of anti-Xa activity); 1 mg protamine per 1 mg enoxaparin given within 8 hours. Provide supportive care and manage bleeding.
